Definition: of Hebrew origin (H348); Jezabel (i.e. Jezebel), a Tyrian woman (used as a synonym of a termagant or false teacher):--Jezabel.
BiblicalUsage: Jezebel is the name John gives to the false teacher at Thyatira, borrowing the name of Ahab's queen. In Revelation 2:20 the Lord says, thou sufferest that woman Jezebel, which calleth herself a prophetess, to teach and to seduce my servants to commit fornication, and to eat things sacrificed unto idols.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the borrowed name is the warning: the old Jezebel led Israel into idolatry, and the new one does the same work inside the church.
RelatedEvents: The Letter to the Church in Thyatira
